title: Polynomial extension increases a module Tor bound by at most the number of variables
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, n and d natural numbers, and M any module over P=A[t₁,...,tₙ]. Suppose Tor_i^A(M,L)=0 for every A-module L and every i>d, using restriction along A → P [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Then Tor_i^P(M,N)=0 for every P-module N and i>d+n. There is no localization, Noetherianity or finite-generation assumption; n=0, d=0, and the zero ring and zero module are included.

source.document: C. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra
source.place: Theorem 4.3.7, pp. 101–102, its exact-sequence argument applied to Tor; https://math.mit.edu/~hrm/palestine/weibel/04-homological_dimension.pdf

proof.text: Induct on n. For n=0, the coefficient map is bijective by MvPolynomial.isEmptyRingEquiv, so the polynomial ring is a localization at the trivial submonoid. Apply the existing localization Tor comparison to close the base case. In the successor case restrict along rename Fin.castSucc. The canonical scalar-restriction composition isomorphism transports hTor, so the induction hypothesis gives bound d+n on the restriction. The successor-variable lemma raises this to d+n+1, equal to d+(n+1).

from.place: Polynomial extension part of the localized polynomial Tor bound; the localization part is proved separately using TorVanishingLocalizedBase.

lean.statement:
theorem polynomial_tor_bound_of_base_tor_bound
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (n : ℕ) (M : ModuleCat.{u} (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)) (d : ℕ)
    (hTor : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A, ∀ i : ℕ, d < i →
      IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj
        ((restrictScalars MvPolynomial.C).obj M)).obj N)) :
    ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A), ∀ i : ℕ, d + n < i →
      IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)) i).obj M).obj N)
